Five times per day for $80$ days, a basketball player has a training session where he practices four free throws in a row and counts the number of baskets he scores. He believes the number of scores in a randomly selected session follows a binomial distribution $B(4, 0.5)$

The frequency distribution of scores and the expected number of observations under the hypothesis that the scores follow the stated binomial distribution are summarized below.

| Number of Scores $(y_{i})$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Observed Frequencies $(O_{i})$ | $25$ | $118$ | $139$ | $93$ | $25$ |
| Expected Frequencies $(E_{i})$ | $25$ | $100$ | $150$ | $100$ | $25$ |

A chi-square goodness of fit test is conducted at the $1%$ significance level with the following null and alternative hypotheses:

- $H_{0}$: The observed distribution can be modeled as $B(4, 0.5)$
- $H_{1}$: The observed distribution cannot be modeled as $B(4, 0.5)$

The table below gives the values of $w$ that satisfy $P(W \ge w) = q$, where $W∼χ^{2}(ν)$.

| $ν∖q$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.010$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $3$ | $6.251$ | $7.815$ | $9.348$ | $11.345$ | $12.838$ |
| $4$ | $7.779$ | $9.488$ | $11.143$ | $13.277$ | $14.860$ |
| $5$ | $9.236$ | $11.070$ | $12.832$ | $15.086$ | $16.750$ |

Using this information, select the options that make the following statements true.

Rounded to two decimal places, the test statistic is {{field-1}}.

The number of degrees of freedom for this test is $ν =$ {{field-2}}.

At the $1%$ significance level, there is {{field-3}} evidence to reject the null hypothesis.
